source.title: Lunar Polar Illumination — average solar illumination, 85S-90S, 60 m/px
source.organization: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center — Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA)
source.citation: Mazarico, E., Neumann, G.A., Smith, D.E., Zuber, M.T., Torrence, M.H. (2011). Illumination conditions of the lunar polar regions using LOLA topography. Icarus 211, 1066-1081. doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030

interpretation.variable: Average fraction of time the solar disc is visible
interpretation.temporalMeaning: Long-term average over hourly timesteps spanning one lunar nutation cycle (~18.6 years). NOT a day-by-day time series.

selectedSite.name: Best-lit 60 m pixel within 20 km of Shackleton centre (used as the fictional SELENE-1 site)

notes: SELENE-1 is fictional; only the illumination fraction comes from NASA data.
Illumination fraction is not electrical power. Panel size and efficiency are game assumptions (see src/lib/nasa/energyModel.ts).
